To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the band offset between GeSn and SiGeSn can significantly improve the subthreshold swing of a TFET with gate overlapped p+ source, that compressive strain improves the performance of GeSn/SigeSn TFETs while tensile strain degrades them, and that the misalignment between pn junction and hetero interface degrades the TFET performance.
the conduction band offset and the energy difference between light hole bands of two materials are the key parameters for n channel and p channel TFETs, respectively.
the performance of a hetero junction TFETS depends mainly on the direct conduction or valance band offsets, the band to band tunnel parameters and on the strain in the channel material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the band offset engineering in hetero TFET structures.
the design of hetero TFET devices with band offsets that can be controlled by the material parameters of the hetero system and strain engineering.
the development of GeSn/SigeSn hetero junction TFETS with high on/off current ratios and steep SSs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GeSn/SiTn hetero TFET with compressively strained GeSn has the potential to outperform the Ge/SiTn heterojunction TFET. Proc. SPIE 10357,
strain engineering of the GeSn channel material is a promising route to enhance the device performance.
the band offsets in GeSn/SiSnGe TFETs have a significant influence on the subthreshold slope and that the performance is strongly affected by the alignment of the hetero and pn junctions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the band offset engineering and strain engineering of the GeSn/SiTn hetero junction can significantly improve the performance of GeSn TFETs.
the GeSn SiGe hetero TFET is a promising candidate to achieve sub 60 mV/dec subthreshold swing.
the GeSn/SigeSn TFETs are a promising candidate for future low power applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
band offset engineering can be used to improve TFET performance, and that compressive strain can widen the design space for GeSn/Si based hetero TFET applications.

hetero junction TFETS with band offsets can outperform conventional TFETs and that the design space for hetero junction TFets with band offsets can be significantly expanded by applying strain engineering.
the design of TFETs with high SS requires the careful engineering of the band offsets and strain in the material system.
